You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From c17c3dc9d08b9aad9a55a1e53f205187972f448e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hugh Dickins <hughd@google.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2020 17:42:17 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] uprobes: __replace_page() avoid BUG in munlock_vma_page()

syzbot crashed on the VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(PageTail) in munlock_vma_page(), when
called from uprobes __replace_page().  Which of many ways to fix it?
Settled on not calling when PageCompound (since Head and Tail are equals
in this context, PageCompound the usual check in uprobes.c, and the prior
use of FOLL_SPLIT_PMD will have cleared PageMlocked already).

Fixes: 5a52c9df62b4 ("uprobe: use FOLL_SPLIT_PMD instead of FOLL_SPLIT")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: Hugh Dickins <hughd@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Reviewed-by: Srikar Dronamraju <srikar@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Acked-by: Song Liu <songliubraving@fb.com>
Acked-by: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Cc: "Kirill A. Shutemov" <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>	[5.4+]
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/alpine.LSU.2.11.2008161338360.20413@eggly.anvils
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/kernel/events/uprobes.c b/kernel/events/uprobes.c
index 649fd53dc9ad..0e18aaf23a7b 100644
--- a/kernel/events/uprobes.c
+++ b/kernel/events/uprobes.c
@@ -205,7 +205,7 @@ static int __replace_page(struct vm_area_struct *vma, unsigned long addr,
 		try_to_free_swap(old_page);
 	page_vma_mapped_walk_done(&pvmw);
 
-	if (vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED)
+	if ((vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED) && !PageCompound(old_page))
 		munlock_vma_page(old_page);
 	put_page(old_page);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `kernel/events/uprobes.c`**
   - **Line Change**: The condition for calling `munlock_vma_page(old_page)` has been modified. 
   - **Original Code**: 
     ```c
     if (vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED)
     ```
   - **Modified Code**: 
     ```c
     if ((vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED) && !PageCompound(old_page))
     ```
   - **Explanation**: The new condition checks if the `vma` is locked and also ensures that `old_page` is not a compound page (i.e., it is not a head or tail page of a compound page). This change prevents the `BUG` that was occurring in `munlock_vma_page()` when it was called with a compound page.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `uprobes.c` directly addresses a bug reported by syzbot, which was triggered by the `munlock_vma_page()` function when it encountered a compound page. By adding the check for `!PageCompound(old_page)`, the patch ensures that `munlock_vma_page()` is only called for non-compound pages, thus preventing the crash and maintaining the integrity of the virtual memory management in the kernel. This change is a refinement of the previous implementation that used `FOLL_SPLIT_PMD`, which had cleared the `PageMlocked` flag but did not account for the compound nature of the page.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED)
    munlock_vma_page(old_page);
```
Reason:
The `munlock_vma_page()` function is called without checking if `old_page` is a compound page. If `old_page` is a compound page, this leads to a `VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(PageTail)` assertion failure because `munlock_vma_page()` is not designed to handle compound pages correctly, resulting in a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if ((vma->vm_flags & VM_LOCKED) && !PageCompound(old_page))
    munlock_vma_page(old_page);
```
Reason:
The patch adds a check to ensure that `munlock_vma_page()` is only called if `old_page` is not a compound page. This prevents the assertion failure by ensuring that the function is only invoked for regular pages, thus avoiding the crash.
